reasoning_traces.think:
The core operators derive from the interplay between scientific inquiry and institutional resistance. The 'truth discovery' primitive models how empirical data (CTE) challenges established norms (NFL practices), modeled as a Bayesian update with adversarial priors. The 'epistemic cost' primitive captures the utility loss when truth conflicts with profit motives, reflecting a game-theoretic equilibrium where institutions may rationally suppress evidence. The 'cognitive dissonance' primitive reflects the psychological friction in communication contexts—particularly in adversarial settings like courtrooms—where identity mismatches impede effective knowledge transfer. These primitives form a dual structure: one of epistemic evolution (truth vs. suppression) and one of behavioral friction (identity vs. context). Failure modes include confirmation bias in institutional narratives and misinterpretation of scientific findings due to cultural dissonance.
